rubrics.intent_basis: Stored literal terms are converted to Atom at every LUT construction and overwrite site. This item covers the independently removable integer/general numeric literal responsibility, not every operation sharing the conversion helper.

rubrics.criterion: Eliminate the obsolete integer/general numeric literal implementation across value, path, and update dispatch so no unreachable duplicate implementation of this operation remains in the supported producer/consumer flow.
rubrics.acceptance: Remove the dead Int/Num execution body and associated obsolete path/update cases, or consistently unify producers and consumers using an equivalent representation. insufficient_repairs: Renaming or moving the obsolete Int/Num body, preserving its outputs without removing redundancy, or only cleaning a different operation.

rubrics.intent_basis: Final Compiler::term Num emits Atom(Literal::Num) only after isize parsing fails; lower::value also converts any raw numeric builder form before storage.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Literal::value reparses a Num as isize even though a successful parse would have produced Int earlier; its success branch is dead under the supported producer chain.
rubrics.criterion: Eliminate the unreachable second integer-parse path, whether by deleting it or by consistently redesigning numeric production and evaluation without dormant duplicate conversion.

Integer/general-number semantics remain supported; no particular enum variant, integer representation, or number of genuinely reachable optimized paths is required.
insufficient_repairs: Keeping the reparse under a renamed helper or adding a test that merely demonstrates numeric behavior.

rubrics.intent_basis: CallDef catch modes are converted by finalize::term from CatchOne/CatchAll to Resolve(false/true) at publication.
rubrics.baseline_defect: def_run retains CatchOne and CatchAll runtime branches alongside Resolve although normal published calls use Resolve for both catch modes.
rubrics.criterion: Eliminate dormant duplicate catch execution across finalization and runtime dispatch.
rubrics.acceptance: Published call states and runtime catch handling agree without unreachable duplicate CatchOne/CatchAll or Resolve execution. Either representation, or another coherent redesign, may be used. Distinct reachable Inline/Throw behavior is retained; no required surviving variant or fixed number of live handlers is imposed.
insufficient_repairs: Rename or relocate catch handlers while an unreachable duplicate catch executor remains. Retaining a formerly old variant in a consistent live redesign is not itself a failure.

rubrics.intent_basis: fold::fold starts with Input and sends all subsequent frames through continuation::push, which transforms Output to Resume before storage; continuation::next handles Resume tails.
rubrics.baseline_defect: fold::fold retains the old Output consumer block even though stack pops can now only see Input or Resume; frame processing and iterator-tail decisions remain duplicated across two consumer bodies.
rubrics.criterion: Eliminate the unreachable pending-output consumer and its duplicate projection/queue implementation across continuation and fold.
rubrics.acceptance: Actual stack producers and pending-output consumption agree, with no dormant alternative consumer caused by Output-to-Resume normalization. Removing either obsolete representation or consistently redesigning state production/consumption qualifies. Iterator tails, errors and optional projection remain supported; exact variant names, module placement and a single literal consumer function are not required.
insufficient_repairs: Move the obsolete pending-output arm without resolving producer/consumer reachability, or create nominally reachable duplicate machinery solely to retain unused code.
